Oakhurst Components Ltd is showing early signs of strain on a large exposure. As at 2026-08-31 the buyer had 5 open invoices with Nordhaven Trade Credit (CL05), the worst of them INV001413 at €329,100 and 25 days past due, with a further four totalling €1,220,700 not yet due. Total open exposure of €1,549,800 already exceeds the €1,450,000 credit limit held on this buyer, an overage of roughly €99,800. Only one settled invoice exists, paid on time, so the file is flagged as insufficient_history and no payment trend can be established. On 2026-09-20, Business Dispatch reported that workers at the Birmingham plant staged a protest over delayed wage payments, with union representatives warning of further action if dues are not cleared.

The score is 47.7, placing the buyer in the Watch band, with a PD of 0.3767. The trace is 0.65 x 33.3 (payment, 25 DPD) + 0.35 x 74.3 (news) = 47.7, giving a weighted payment contribution of 21.7 and a weighted news contribution of 26.0. The adjudicator agreed with caveats. The key caveat is that the band turns almost entirely on the news item: it supplies 26.0 of the 47.7 points, and without it the payment score of 21.7 alone would fall in the Healthy band. That severity 5 signal rests on a two-sentence article from a single publication with no corroborating source, though the entity match is direct rather than via parent and the Birmingham location is consistent. Two further caveats weigh the other way: the payment score reads only the 25 DPD and is structurally blind to the limit breach, and the payment snapshot of 2026-08-31 predates the wage-delay report of 2026-09-20 by about three weeks, so it may understate current condition.

The recommendation for Nordhaven Trade Credit (CL05) is FREEZE on limit LIM0036. The current limit of €1,450,000 is held unchanged as the revised limit, a change of 0, because the buyer is already owed at or above the limit and there is nothing left to cut. Expected loss is €417,854 both before and after the action, and the maximum liability constraint does not bind. PD of 0.3767 sits above the target of 0.25, so the freeze holds the line rather than bringing the file back to appetite.

Two things would lift this file. First, refreshing the payment position: the 2026-08-31 snapshot should be updated before the verdict is relied on, and clearance of the €329,100 past-due invoice with the €1,220,700 pipeline settling as it falls due would bring exposure back within the €1,450,000 limit and build the payment history the file currently lacks. Second, resolving the news signal: confirmation against a second source, or evidence that the delayed wages have been cleared and the union action lifted, would address the concern that more than half the score rests on an uncorroborated single-publication stub. With the news component removed or stood down, the payment score of 21.7 alone would fall in the Healthy band; bringing PD from 0.3767 toward the 0.25 target is what would support any move off the frozen €1,450,000 line.
